issues.body:
The new gate `return explicit[0] if explicit[0] in ROLE_LABELS else None` makes ROLE_LABELS the authoritative allowlist for explicit roles, but the catalog is incomplete on arrival.

`orchestration/routing.toml` configures seven roles via `[[route]] role = "..."`: impl (110), site (122), ci (144), research (149), docs (154), review (164), soundness (170). ROLE_LABELS lists six — `review` is missing. The review route is load-bearing: model_chain [opus5, opus], agent registry-reviewer, escalate = true, and it is asserted live at scripts/route-resolve.py:178 (`review -> opus/escalate`).

Consequence for an issue labelled `role:review`: _role() returns None, so triage() takes the `if role:` branch not at all — no role is added, ready is False, `status:ready` is removed and `status:untriaged` added. The issue is permanently un-promotable and never dispatches, even though route-resolve/policy-resolve would route it correctly. The registry's own review/escalation lane silently starves.

Same defect for `role:perf`, emitted by scripts/curate-frontier.py:319 (`role_for()` returns "role:perf" for kind:perf) and present in that script's own label fixture at line 827.

Note also that when _role() returns None the pre-existing role:* label is NOT stripped — the strip lives inside `if role:` — so the rejected label persists on the issue indefinitely.
issues.fix_hint: Do not hand-maintain a second role list. Either (a) derive the catalog from orchestration/routing.toml's `[[route]] role = ...` set (parse it once, attach color/description as presentation-only metadata keyed off that set), or (b) if a literal must stay, add `review` and `perf` now AND add a self-test that parses routing.toml and asserts `{r['role'] for r in doc['route'] if 'role' in r} <= set(ROLE_LABELS)`, so the two can never drift again. Whichever you pick, make the drift check fail red rather than relying on review to notice.
issues.title: ROLE_LABELS omits configured roles `review` and `perf`; _role() now rejects them, starving the review lane

issues.body:
`chk("all derived roles have labels", derived_roles <= set(ROLE_LABELS), True)` builds derived_roles from ROLE_BY_KIND.values(), ROLE_BY_TYPE.values(), the UI/INFRA surface labels and area:dispatch. That evaluates to {docs, research, ci, site, soundness, impl}, which is exactly set(ROLE_LABELS) — the assertion passes.

But every one of those roles arrives via the *derivation* path, which this diff did not touch. The diff changed the *explicit* path (`role:*` already on the issue). No derivation ever produces `review` or `perf`, so the check is structurally incapable of catching the blocker above: the catalog can be missing any number of explicit-only roles and this test stays green.

So the guard added to protect the new gate does not exercise the new gate's risk surface. `unknown explicit role rejected` is genuinely non-vacuous (it flips red on pre-diff code), but it only proves the mechanism fires — it says nothing about the catalog being complete, which is the property that actually matters.
issues.fix_hint: Add an assertion over the roles the *consumers* use, not the ones triage derives: parse orchestration/routing.toml (tomllib, as route-resolve.py already does) and assert every configured `role` is a ROLE_LABELS key. Keep the derived-roles check too — it is a useful separate invariant — but it must not be the only one.
issues.title: New self-test covers the unchanged derivation branch, not the changed explicit-role branch

issues.body:
The reconcile loop creates only what `--role-labels` emits: the six `role:*` labels. But triage() can also add `status:ready`, `status:untriaged` and `needs:area`. Nothing in this workflow reconciles those, and no bootstrap creates them for this repo — set-up-account.yml:621 creates only status:pending and account; worker.yml:1125 creates labels on *target* repos, not here.

The adds are emitted `sorted`, so the loop order is needs:area < role:X < status:Y. If the `role:*` add succeeds and the following `status:*` add then fails (label absent, or a transient 5xx — these mutations are deliberately not wrapped in gh_retry), errexit aborts the step BEFORE the remove loop. Result: the new `role:soundness` is on the issue and the old `role:impl` was never removed — two role:* labels.

That is precisely the ambiguous set the single-role invariant exists to prevent (scripts/triage.py:95-96), and route-resolve/policy-resolve reject it. Under the old `|| true` the remove loop still ran and left a consistent single role. So the step comment — "preserving the issue's existing role rather than leaving it roleless" — is only half true: it does prevent roleless, but it newly admits role-ambiguous. It fails closed (dispatch refuses an ambiguous issue), hence major rather than blocker, but it is a regression the comment asserts does not exist.
issues.fix_hint: Make the reconcile cover every label triage can add, not just the role subset — extend the catalog (or add a second `--status-labels` emitter) to include status:ready, status:untriaged and needs:area. Alternatively make the apply phase atomic with respect to the role swap: compute the final label set and apply it in one `gh issue edit` call, so a partial failure cannot leave two role:* labels. Also update the step comment so it states the guarantee actually provided.
issues.title: Reconcile covers only role labels, so dropping `|| true` can strand two role:* labels on the issue

issues.body:
For labels {role:impl, area:worker, priority:P2, from:agent}, SEC_KEYWORDS matches "worker" and _role() short-circuits to "soundness" at the top of the function — before the explicit-role branch this diff modified. Both new checks therefore produce the same result before and after the change and cannot flip red on it.

They have value as regression coverage of the add/remove plan shape, so this is not a demand to delete them — but they should not be read as validating the diff, and the comment above them ("Exact regression") overstates what they pin.

`trust role replacement adds before remove` is additionally misnamed: it asserts `"role:soundness" in r["add"]` and `"role:impl" in r["remove"]` — set membership, not ordering. triage() returns unordered sets; the actual ordering guarantee comes from the workflow emitting `sorted()` and running the add loop before the remove loop, none of which this test touches.
issues.fix_hint: Rename to something like `trust role replacement plans add+remove` to match what it asserts, and add a case that exercises the changed branch — e.g. an explicit role on a NON-trust area, where SEC_KEYWORDS does not short-circuit. If you want real ordering coverage, assert on the sorted CLI output (`sorted(add)` puts role:* before status:*), which is the property the shell loop actually depends on.
issues.title: `trust role replacement` checks pass identically on pre-diff code (vacuous for this change)

issues.body:
`done < <(python3 scripts/triage.py --role-labels)` runs the generator in a process substitution, whose exit status is not observed by `set -euo pipefail` (and is not covered by pipefail either, since it is not a pipeline). If that invocation fails — ImportError, a bad argparse change, a traceback — the while loop reads zero lines, creates nothing, and the step proceeds to compute and apply a plan.

The step's comment claims "A create failure aborts the step", which is true for `gh label create` specifically, but the reader will take it as covering the whole reconcile. It does not cover the generator. Recovery is indirect: a subsequent `gh issue edit --add-label` for a nonexistent label errors client-side and errexit then fires — so it does fail closed, but only after partial application (see the major above), and with a confusing error.
issues.fix_hint: Materialise the catalog first so the failure is observed directly: `catalog=$(python3 scripts/triage.py --role-labels)` (command substitution IS covered by errexit), then feed the loop with `done <<< "$catalog"`. Tighten the comment to say which failures abort the step.
issues.title: Process substitution hides a `--role-labels` failure from errexit

issues.body: The workflow parses this output with `IFS=$'\t' read -r label color description`, so the TAB-separated, one-record-per-line shape and the `role:` name prefix are a real cross-file contract. `_self_test()` asserts on ROLE_LABELS as a dict but never on the rendered `--role-labels` output, so a description gaining a tab or newline, or the `role:` prefix being dropped, would break the workflow with nothing red in the gate.
issues.fix_hint: Add a check that renders the catalog the way main() does and asserts each line splits into exactly 3 TAB fields, the first starts with `role:`, and no field contains a tab or newline.
issues.title: `--role-labels` output contract is untested

verdict.summary:
The intent is right (reconcile the role-label catalog before applying a plan; stop swallowing add failures with `|| true`), and the model-marker removals from both file headers match the model-agnostic provenance rule. But the new ROLE_LABELS catalog is a SECOND hand-maintained source of truth for a set that orchestration/routing.toml already owns, and it is already out of sync on the very first commit: routing.toml configures 7 roles (impl, site, ci, research, docs, review, soundness) while ROLE_LABELS lists 6 — `role:review` is absent. scripts/curate-frontier.py:319 also emits `role:perf`, likewise absent. Because _role() now returns None for any explicit role not in ROLE_LABELS, an issue carrying `role:review` (a live route resolving to registry-reviewer with escalate=true, self-tested at scripts/route-resolve.py:178) is demoted to role=None -> never ready -> permanently status:untriaged. The review/escalation lane starves. This fails closed rather than open, so it is not a security hole, but it is a real functional regression in the trust plane's own review lane.

The accompanying self-test does not catch this because it is scoped to the wrong branch: `all derived roles have labels` checks only ROLE_BY_KIND/ROLE_BY_TYPE/UI/INFRA derivations — the path the diff did NOT change — and never asserts that the roles routing.toml configures are representable, which is exactly the path the diff DID change. The two `trust role replacement` checks are vacuous with respect to this diff: SEC_KEYWORDS forces soundness for area:worker both before and after the change, so they pass identically on the pre-diff code, and `adds before remove` asserts set membership, not ordering — the actual ordering guarantee lives in two shell loops that no test exercises.
